messages:
leigh: Quick doc bug: public API ref and OpenAPI disagree for POST /v1/generate. Ref shows "max_tokens" and response as "choices[0].text". Runtime and OpenAPI return "max_new_tokens" and "output: [{text,...}]". This is breaking our curl/js examples and some customers reported integration failures.

owen: Where's the authoritative schema? OpenAPI or runtime? We should update both.

taylor: OpenAPI is in openapi/generate.yaml in the repo  it already has output[] and max_new_tokens. The markdown docs (content/api/generate.md) were out of sync: an old snippet slipped back in. I'll patch the markdown and regenerate snippets.

leigh: Minimal repro I used (staging):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood/fast-1","max_new_tokens":10,"prompt":"Define idempotence"}'
```
Response:
```
{"id":"gen_789","model":"redwood/fast-1","output":[{"text":"Idempotence means...","type":"text"}]}
```

taylor: Plan: (1) make canonical param "max_new_tokens" in the param table, (2) swap examples to the "output" array shape, (3) update the snippet generator mapping so raw HTTP shows max_new_tokens, (4) add a short migration/deprecation note mapping old "max_tokens" -> "max_new_tokens", (5) add example-validation tests against openapi/generate.yaml to catch regressions.

owen: Also update SDK snippet renderer to show both raw HTTP (max_new_tokens) and an SDK helper example that contains a deprecation comment if the SDK still accepts max_tokens. Add a tiny test that runs the example through the snippet linter.

leigh: I'll open a PR with the docs patch + tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1188

docs-bot: docs-ci: example-validation failed for content/api/generate.md (schema mismatch). See https://ci.internal.redwood/9999 :x:

taylor: Once PR merges, please ping #support with a short blurb and link to the migration note so customers aren't surprised.

owen: Will do. Posting after merge. :thumbsup:
